purpose: Source-linked qualitative evidence for all thirteen core method/system studies. Six selected comparisons appear in the survey evidence table; this is not an exhaustive experimental extraction or a new benchmark.

observations.observation: TIS uses recorded rollout probabilities to bound correction in hybrid and quantized rollout settings; comparisons examine stability and downstream learning.
observations.limit: Truncated correction is a biased surrogate; the experiments do not imply equivalence to response-level importance sampling.

observations.observation: Unified FP8 precision flow and coordinated quantization granularity address learner-rollout inconsistency, with accuracy and efficiency evaluated in the reported stack.
observations.limit: Path-specific consistency does not establish bitwise identity across arbitrary engines or formats.

observations.observation: The stack combines W8A8 rollout, attention/KV scaling, synchronization, and adopted TIS/MIS; v2 also explores end-to-end FP8.
observations.limit: Learner precision and component settings vary by experiment; system-level gains do not isolate every component.

observations.observation: Longer-run behavior under TIS motivates ACR; invariant scaling addresses quantized weight-update visibility.
observations.limit: Within-paper setting; not a universal failure horizon.

observations.observation: Rollout-aligned QAT and sequence-level TBPO are evaluated jointly and through component ablations for quantized MoE reasoning RL.
observations.limit: The numerical and objective components act on different objects; QAT emulation is distinct from native low-precision arithmetic.

observations.observation: An adaptive mixture of uncorrected and importance-weighted gradients responds to mismatch diagnostics; the paper studies autoregressive and diffusion models.
observations.limit: The adapted quantity is the estimator mixture, not precision; diffusion likelihood semantics differ from the autoregressive formulation.

observations.observation: Asymmetric weight QAT and rollout residual compensation show complementary gains.
observations.limit: Ablation does not establish universal necessity or superiority of asymmetric QAT.

observations.observation: Advantage-guided probability adjustment regulates discrepancy through update influence; robustness and bidirectional-control ablations examine the reported FP8 regimes.
observations.limit: Regulation around a reference range is not unconditional minimization of discrepancy and does not establish native FP4 transfer.

observations.observation: Shared-objective corrections are compared; top-k behavior reconstruction is used; composition is tested under lag.
observations.limit: Conditional score centering is not recovery of the on-policy trajectory distribution.

observations.observation: Signed clipping effects motivate BF16-reference calibration; main GRPO endpoints select the best average checkpoint over 500 steps.
observations.limit: Best checkpoint differs from final checkpoint or time-to-quality.

observations.observation: Local directional diagnostics motivate gating and repair; token-wise predictiveness is restricted in the routing-conditioned MoE analysis.
observations.limit: Population directional trends do not ensure token-independent contraction.

observations.observation: Rollout-guided FP4 rounding and compact quantization-information transfer are evaluated for MoE learning, including efficiency and component comparisons.
observations.limit: The local rounding argument is not a global policy-divergence guarantee; storage, transport, and state matching remain system dependencies.

observations.observation: Selective protection improves INT4 KV fidelity and learning under the retained TIS recipe.
observations.limit: Colocated quota-based partial collection; generation and optimization alternate.
